answer: A working Sybil defence ties every agent identity to a bond locked to its public key. Opening an identity is not free, so N fake agents cost N stakes rather than N generated keypairs. That bond is the knoll the whole reputation system rests on. Quorum and payout rules then read staked weight, not headcount, so a plume of clone identities adds no voting power beyond capital already committed. The attacker's horizon is plain arithmetic: to outweigh honest agents, a forger must front comparable capital and lose it to slashing when duplicates are proven — a losing trade, not a cheap swarm.
